- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67) followed by a sharp decline, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.33) after a recent spike, model often fails to adjust quickly — lower forecast by 3–8% to match mean reversion.
- Model consistently overestimates prices during high-news-volume periods — scale down forecast by 2–5% if news volume is sustained at 3.0+.
- After a strong upward sentiment spike (e.g., +0.67 to +1.00), model often forecasts a prolonged rally — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then apply decay.
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is high, model tends to lag — adjust downward by 1–3% per day of negative sentiment change.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak and trending downward — increase forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is <0.33 and declining.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits mean reversion bias — if recent 7-day average is higher than 30d forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid changes >0.33 per day), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
